 J U D G M E N T

The petitioner has filed this claim petition U/S.166 of M.V. Act against the respondents claiming compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- on account of injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 2.7.2018 at about 8.45 a.m. the petitioner was crossing the road on Aladamara Road, near Government School, Papareddypalya, Nagarabhavi, Bengaluru, at that time, Suzuki Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EX-3585 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety of others and dashed against the petitioner.
Due to the impact, she fell down and sustained grievous injuries all over the body.
Immediately she was shifted to Essential hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she was admitted as an inpatient.

3. Further the contention of the petitioner is that, prior to the accident, she was hale and healthy,
aged about 7 years, studying in 1st standard.
On account of the injuries she is permanently disabled and she lost happiness, physically and mentally.
The accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Contending the above facts, she prays to grant for compensation with interest and cost.
4. In response to the petition notice, the respondent No.1 has not appeared before the court and placed exparte.
The respondent No.2 has appeared before the court through its counsel and filed its respective written statement.
5. The brief contents of written statement of respondent No.2 are as under:
The respondent in its written statement averred that, the claim petition filed by the petitioner is not maintainable either in law or on facts.
Further contended that neither the owner of the vehicle nor the jurisdictional police have complied mandatory provisions u/s 134 and S.158 (6) of the MV Act.
Further admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of vehicle bearing No.KA-01-EX-3585 and its Kum.

Vedashree P vs Shri Murali on 20 April, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35270277/
2 validity.
Further contended that the rider of the offending vehicle had no valid and effective driving licence to ride the above said vehicle at the time of accident.
Further contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Further denied the age, studying in 1st standard of the petitioner as alleged in the claim petition.
Contending the above facts, prays to dismiss the claim petition with cost.

6. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues were framed:
1.

Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of Suzuki Motor Cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EX- 3585 on 2.7.2018 at about 8.45 a.m. on Aladamara Road, Near Government School,
Papareddypalya, Nagarabhavi, Bengaluru?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for? If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3.
What order or award?

7. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as PW1 and got marked the documents as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12 and doctor is examined as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P13 to Ex.P16.
8.
To disprove the case of the petitioner and to prove the defence, the respondent has not examined any witness nor marked any documents on its behalf.
9. Heard the arguments.

10. My findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: In the Partly Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following:
R E A S O N S 11. ISSUE NO.1:- During the course of arguments, the learned counsel for the petitioner argued by reiterating the contents of petition and also evidence put forth by PW1 & PW2.
Further he argued that, the petitioner has proved his case as contended in the petition by producing oral and documentary evidence.
Accordingly, he prays to allow the petition.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for the respondent No.2 has argued by denying the manner of the accident as alleged in the petition and contended that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
Accordingly, he prays to dismiss the petition as against this respondent.

sentences.text: On rival contention urged by both the counsel, I, intend to discuss the merits of the case.
14. In order to prove the case, the father of the petitioner has examined as P.W.1 and he has stated in his evidence by reiterating the contents of petition.

To substantiate the said contention he has produced prosecution papers and the same are marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P7 such as FIR with complaint, spot mahazar, rough sketch, statement of witnesses, IMV report, wound certificate and charge sheet respectively.
15.
On perusal of FIR with complaint, complaint has lodged by Panduranga, son of Sangappa on 2.7.2018.
Based on the complaint case has been registered against the rider of the motor cycle in Cr.No.130/2018 by Kamakshipalya Traffic police for the offences punishable u/s 279 and 337 of IPC.
Ex . P2 and Ex.P3 are the mahazar and sketch also reveals the scene of occurrence and it corroborates Ex.P1.
Ex.P4 is the statement of witnesses also corroborative the evidence of PW1.
Ex.P5 IMV report reveals that the cause of accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle.
Ex. P6

is wound certificate reveals the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and on perusal of charge sheet at Ex.P7 reveals that after investigation I.O. has filed charge sheet against the offending vehicle driver for the offences punishable U/s 279, 337 and 338 of IPC.
16.

The respondent No.2 has contended in its written statement that accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner and the alleged vehicle was not at all involved in the accident, but to substantiate the said fact, the respondent has not led any rebuttal evidence to prove its defence,
moreover he has not challenged the charge sheet filed against the rider of the motor cycle.
On the other hand, petitioner has proved her case through oral and documentary evidence.

17. In addenda of this, in a claim for compensation U/S.166 of MV Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and the standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by Hon'ble Apex Court in the decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 (Kusum and others Vs. Satbir and others).

sentences.text: 18. Looking to the oral evidence of PW1 and the documents placed before the court I am of the opinion that, petitioner has proved her case that the accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-01-EX-3585.
Hence, I answer this issue in the affirmative.
19. ISSUE NO.2:- PW1 being the father of the petitioner has stated in his evidence that petitioner has met with an accident on 2.7.2018 at about 8.45 a.m. and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately she was taken to Essential hospital, Bengaluru, wherein she took the treatment as inpatient.

To substantiate the said fact, PW1 has produced wound certificate at Ex.P6, which reveals the following injuries;
1) Open Fracture both bones of right leg 2)Multiple abrasions over the right leg and foot Kum.
Vedashree P vs Shri Murali on 20 April, 2019

Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35270277/
4 20.
The doctor is of the opinion that the said injury No.1 is grievous in nature and the injury No.2 is simple in nature.
PW1 has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which reveals that petitioner took the treatment as inpatient from 2.7.2018 to 6.7.2018.
Dr.Sukesh Shetty B. has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained Type I Open fracture both bones of right leg.
She underwent surgery in the form of CRIF with Tens nails.
He has produced Ex.P13 to Ex.P16 such as case sheet, true copy of MLC register extract, copy of Police intimation and X-rays.

Considering the oral evidence of PW1 and PW2 and the documents placed before the court, I am of the opinion that the petitioner might have sustained pain and agony,
for which, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of pain and sufferings.
22.
The case of the petitioner is that, she was hale and healthy at the time of accident, aged about 7 years.
Due to the accidental injuries she has suffered a lot.
The petitioner has produced discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, which reveals that petitioner took the treatment as inpatient from 2.7.2018 to 6.7.2018.
PW1 has also produced study certificate of the petitioner, which is marked at Ex.P11, which discloses that the petitioner was studying in 1st Standard.
As the petitioner has sustained Type I open fracture of both bones of right leg and admitted as an inpatient after that she might have taken rest and treatment atleast for two months.
During the said period either father or mother, one has to look after their daughter by leaving their work.
So, I deem it fit to grant Rs.20,000/- under the head of inconvenience caused to the parents during the treatment period.
Therefore, Rs.20,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.
23. The contention of PW1 is that, they have spent Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses.
She has produced the Inpatient bill marked at Ex.P9 to the extent of Rs.80,000/- and medical bills at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.7,153/- supported with prescriptions.
Considering the above facts, I deem it just and reasonable to grant compensation of Rs.87,153/- rounded up to Rs.87,160/- under the head of medical expenses.

24. Further contention of the PW1 is that, prior to the accident, petitioner was hale and healthy,
aged about 7 years, student.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has sustained pain, she cannot do her regular activities.
25. PW2 Dr.Sukeh Shetty B. has stated in his evidence that he has examined the petitioner on 6.3.201.
He has assessed the disability of right lower limb at 30% and whole body disability is 10%.
Therefore, the disability of the petitioner shall be considered as 10%of the whole body.

26. At this juncture this Court has relied the decision reported in 2013 ACJ 2445 in between Mallikarjun Vs. Divisional Manager, National Insurance Co.Ltd.,and another, which reads like thus;
Quantum - Injury - Principles of assessment - Assessment of compensation in case of children suffering disability - Apex Court observed that appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10 per cent and up to 30 per cent to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; up to 60 percent, Rs.4,00,000; up to 90 per cent, Rs.5,00,000 and above 90 per cent, it should be Rs.6,00,000; for permanent Kum.

5 disability up to 10 per cent, it should be Rs.1,00,000, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take a different yardstick.

27. In the instant case the disability of the petitioner shall be considered as 10% of whole body, so,
up to 10% disability it should be Rs.1,00,000/-.
Therefore, Rs.1,00,000/- is granted under the head of disability.
28. PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accident petitioner took the treatment as inpatient and also as outpatient.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P8, it reveals that the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient from 2.7.2018 to 6.7.2018 and also outpatient.

So,
one must attend her during the above said period.

Considering the above facts and looking to the period of hospitalization, I deem it just and reasonable to grant for compensation of Rs.20,000/-under the head of amenities, attendant, conveyance, food and nourishment etc.,
29.
PW2 has stated in his evidence that petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants, which could cost around Rs.20,000/-.
Relying on the opinion of the doctor it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.20,000/- towards future medication.

30. Considering the above facts and circumstances of the case and for the above reason, I am of the opinion that the petitioner is entitled for total compensation under the following heads:
Sl.
No . Compensation heads Amount 1. Pain and suffering Rs. 40,000-00 2. Loss of income during laid period Rs. 20,000-00  and rest period 3. Medical expenses Rs. 87,160-00 4.
Permanent disability Rs.1,00,000-00 5. Loss of amenities, Attendant, Rs. 20,000-00  Nourishment and conveyance
charges
6. Future medication Rs. 20,000-00
LIABILITY:

As I have already discussed in issue No.1 that the accident occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EX-3585.
32.
The respondent No.2 in its written statement has admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of motor cycle bearing No.KA-01-EX-3585 and its validity.
Therefore, respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.2 alone is liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner with interest @ 8% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
Accordingly, I answer the issue No.2 in the partly affirmative.
33. ISSUE NO.3:

sentences.text: The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of MV Act as against the respondents is partly allowed with cost.
The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.2,87,160/- with interest @ 8% p.a. from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance police the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioner with interest at 8% p.a. from the date of petition till its realisation within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.

After deposit of compensation amount together with interest, entire amount shall be kept in FD in the name of petitioner in any nationalized/schedule bank till she attains age of majority and after attaining the age of majority the entire amount shall be released to the petitioner through account payee cheque on proper identification without any further proceedings.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the stenographer online, corrected by me and then pronounced in open court on this 20th day of April 2019).
